=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or clustered arrangement visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem, not clustered at the apex or base)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf consists of multiple leaflets arranged along a central axis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (leaflets arranged in pairs along the rachis with a single terminal leaflet; terminal leaflet visible in some images)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 8 (estimated per leaf; each leaf has approximately 8 pairs of leaflets plus a terminal leaflet, totaling ~17 leaflets per leaf; closest integer from options is 8 for paired count, but full count is ~17; however, per instructions, use integer estimate from 2, 4, 8, etc. — 8 is most appropriate as it reflects the paired structure; note: 17 is not an option, so 8 is best fit for paired count)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are arranged in pairs along the rachis, directly across from each other)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are broadest at the middle and taper to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (apex is sharply pointed)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base of leaflets is gently curved)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs lengthwise with secondary veins branching off at angles)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, run parallel to each other, and are closely packed)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (surface appears matte, not glossy or shiny)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or trichomes on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short compared to leaflet length)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem is firm, brown, and appears lignified, typical of young woody plant)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: brown (stem is dark brown, with some reddish-brown tones)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): ridged (stem surface has slight longitudinal ridges or grooves)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible when stem is broken or damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joints at base of leaflets or petiole; pulvinus not visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no modified stems or leaves functioning as tendrils)
F. Notes: Some leaflets show small holes, likely from mechanical damage or minor abrasion, but no clear evidence of insect herbivory. The seedling is growing against a decaying tree trunk with moist, dark soil. Multiple images confirm consistent morphology across angles.
